review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset labels 1.0 and 0.5 count as INCLUDE; 0.0 counts as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is an observational/retrospective study analyzing complications from 5,851 consecutively induced abortions. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not compare different surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized study comparing conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) vs manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) in 200 women with gestational age <56 days. Meets all criteria: RCT, compares different surgical methods, first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: This is a historical/observational study comparing mortality and morbidity data before and after Roe v Wade using data from National Center for Health Statistics, CDC, and other databases. It is not a randomized controlled trial and does not compare different surgical methods.

This is a randomized trial but compares prostaglandin suppository vs placebo (medical cervical preparation), not different surgical methods. All patients received vacuum aspiration; the intervention is medical preparation, not surgical technique.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized study comparing dilatation and curettage (D&C) vs vacuum aspiration in 420 women at 6-12 weeks gestation. Meets all criteria: RCT, compares different surgical methods, first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration vs electric vacuum aspiration in 84 women at <10 weeks gestation. Meets all criteria: RCT, compares different surgical methods, first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized study comparing manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) vs electric vacuum aspiration (EVA) in 127 women for first trimester abortion. Meets all criteria: RCT, compares different surgical methods, first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: This study compares vacuum aspiration vs classical dilatation and curettage in 47 women, but there is no mention of randomization. The abstract describes groups (23 vs 24) but does not state they were randomly assigned.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized study comparing metal vs flexible plastic cannulae for vacuum aspiration in 300 subjects at 7-10 weeks gestation. While both are vacuum aspiration, the cannulae type represents a different surgical technique. Meets criteria: RCT, compares different surgical methods, first trimester abortion.

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomized trial comparing manual vacuum aspirator vs electric vacuum curettage devices in 114 women undergoing first-trimester abortions. Meets all criteria: RCT, compares different surgical methods, first trimester abortion.
